parallel.requirements: The parallel parent understood the task as a cleanroom reimplementation of the clog executable and identified detailed behavior such as clap-style CLI output, changelog sections, git command patterns, JSON quirks, and file I/O concerns.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent split the task into seven behavior-probing children covering CLI, config, commit parsing, version/header, output, file I/O, and git invocation. Each child was instructed to probe only, while no actor was assigned to produce the implementation.
parallel.implementation: No replacement source, build script, or executable implementation was created. The child work remained behavior discovery and local harness experimentation.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: There was no final integration of findings into a codebase. The submitted artifact contained the original workspace files and executable but no replacement implementation source, and artifact validation was false.
parallel.verification: Parallel verification was fragmented across child probes and never advanced to an evaluator-aligned check of a new implementation. The official evaluation completed but failed during compilation.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The attempt timed out after cancelling active subagents; every delegated probe returned stopped-before-finished and the final artifact could not compile.

serial.requirements: The serial actor worked from the same prompt and eventually discovered important task facts, especially that a `[sections]` table was needed for commits to appear in output.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial run had one actor and no delegation. The same actor retained ownership of probing and any possible implementation work, but did not reach implementation before timeout.
serial.implementation: The serial run produced behavioral observations and test repositories but did not create a replacement implementation source or build path.
serial.integration_and_delivery: There was no component integration step because there were no child components. The submitted artifact was still the original workspace-like tree with no new buildable code.
serial.verification: Serial verification consisted of direct executable probes, including markdown and JSON output checks. It did not verify a replacement binary because none was built.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial run also timed out and officially failed compilation with no tests run, despite reaching stronger local behavioral understanding than the parallel parent consumed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent recognized a cleanroom reimplementation and many detailed behavioral requirements before delegation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor recognized the same cleanroom constraints and later discovered the decisive `[sections]` configuration behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial retained a single evolving requirement picture, while parallel distributed requirement discovery into probes that never returned completed reports.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into seven probing children and no visible implementation owner.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept one main actor with no subagents and no delegation boundary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created a coordination plan around research fan-out; serial had no cross-agent ownership split.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs were self-contained but intentionally scoped to observation and reporting rather than deliverable code or interoperable components.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial carried context forward within the same actor and applied new discoveries directly to later probes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The contrast is not a missing interface contract; it is that parallel placed knowledge acquisition behind child handoffs that never completed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel never moved from behavior probing into constructing a replacement executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also never implemented, but it produced richer direct observations in the main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had the same final implementation gap, but parallel amplified it by allocating all delegated work to probes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent launched active child agents but then cancelled the active turn and received failed stopped-before-finished child results.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; observations were immediately available to the only actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a result lifecycle failure absent from serial.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Multiple children used the same `/tmp/clogtest` area and observed sibling-created or missing files, forcing relocation to unique workspaces.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial created and used its own temporary repositories sequentially within one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had concrete unisolated temporary-state interference; serial did not have cross-agent shared-state interference.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had local probe checks but no integrated verification of a new implementation before official compile failure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had direct behavioral probes but likewise no verification of a replacement executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Neither run reached acceptance verification; parallel's child results were unavailable before closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the run budget with seven live subagents and timed out before implementation or closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but without subagents and with fewer tool calls in the metadata.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both closed by timeout; parallel's budget pressure coincided with unfinished child work and no implementation owner.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcomes are not discordant: both completed evaluator records report compile_failed, solution_passed false, and 0 of 778 tests passed. The concrete process difference is that serial kept probing in one actor and reached useful `[sections]` behavior, while parallel launched seven probe-only children, cancelled them before final handoffs, and had shared temporary workspace interference. Those are adverse parallel coordination patterns but they do not explain an outcome difference because serial also failed to deliver buildable replacement code.
parallel_contributors: Seven child probes were launched with probe-only instructions and no implementation owner.
Active child work was cancelled before complete reports were returned.
Several children encountered shared `/tmp/clogtest` state from concurrent sibling probes.
serial_contributors: Serial had no delegation boundary and discovered the `[sections]` requirement in the main trajectory.
Serial still spent the whole run on probing and did not create replacement source or a build script.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both submissions lacked a new buildable implementation and failed compilation.
Serial had stronger main-thread behavioral notes, but this did not become delivered code.
evaluator_effects: The evaluator outcome for both modes was compile_failed with all tests not run.

candidates.reason: The work split assigned seven children to behavior probing and explicitly kept them from writing implementation code, while no parent or child received ownership of producing the required replacement executable.
candidates.realized_consequence: No replacement implementation files or build script were produced, so the final artifact failed during compilation.
candidates.near_match_reason: The earliest missing owner was for producing the implementation, not for an end-to-end pipeline after implementation ownership already existed.

candidates.reason: There were no separately owned component implementations that needed reconciliation into one coherent implementation.
The run never produced component work ready for final build, packaging, or placement, so assembly ownership is downstream of the missing implementation owner.
The failure was not an unowned transition across implementation, build, test, and delivery stages; implementation itself lacked an owner.
No single mandatory serial preflight gate blocked all productive work; the parent chose broad concurrent probing instead.
The probes were launched concurrently and did not complete as a separate first phase before implementation began; the better boundary is missing implementation ownership and child cancellation.
The indispensable implementation path had no assigned owner at all, so the direct ownership boundary is more specific than underallocation of a known critical path.
Although seven children and a timeout are visible, the directly evidenced failure chain is probe-only ownership plus cancellation, not proof that fan-out breadth independently exhausted the budget.
No single child was assigned a dominant overbroad implementation scope; each assignment was a bounded probing topic.

The child briefs intentionally scoped probing assignments and included the cleanroom constraints; the missing deliverable owner is an orchestration plan problem, not a hidden known requirement omitted from a child's task.
The children were not producing separately owned interoperating components, so no missing file, API, export, or compatibility contract caused incompatible component work.
No completed finding is shown before transfer and then lost, omitted, or truncated at receipt; the children were stopped before final handoffs.
The parent did not receive large completed child reports and fail to reduce them; it received stopped-before-finished errors.
There is no parent action based on a superseded child handoff or workspace state after a newer state was observable.
No incompatible completed child reports reached the parent and remained unadjudicated at an integration decision.
The parent did not make an observable whole-task completion decision; the run ended by cancellation and timeout before a final implementation was accepted.
No retry or replacement child was launched without inherited findings and then observed repeating prior work.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parent launched active child agents, then the trajectory shows an active-turn cancellation and each child result reports that the subagent was stopped before it finished.
candidates.realized_consequence: No completed child reports reached the parent, so delegated behavioral discoveries could not be consumed for implementation.
candidates.near_match_reason: The child results were not completed verifier findings trapped below the parent; they were explicitly interrupted before finishing.

candidates.reason: No complete candidate implementation or mutually compatible component set existed for promotion or packaging before closure.
No child implementation change was merged after verification; there was no final implementation merge at all.
No delegated implementation was completed or retrievable for the parent to join into the final solution.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent; all child tasks were stopped before completing.

The stopped-child terminal state is already captured by Early Child Termination; there is no separate observed post-failure interval where the parent received a failure and failed to reassign or take over.
No completed child result was available to the parent and then ignored; returned child results were failure messages.
The directly visible lifecycle event is active child cancellation before completion, not parent waiting while ignoring available actionable progress.
No children produced competing implementations in different files claiming overlapping behavior or build ownership.
The evidence does not prove two live agents edited the same source or configuration file and had to reconcile that same file.
No non-entry source module produced or actively owned by one agent was wholesale replaced by another.
No required executable, entry-point source, or submitted artifact was replaced while another agent owned or used it.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion overwrote multiple current final outputs or invalidated final-tree provenance.

Multiple live child agents wrote to shared temporary probing state, especially `/tmp/clogtest`, and several children observed unexpected foreign files or missing helper directories before moving to unique workspaces.
candidates.realized_consequence: Child probes lost stable temporary-workspace provenance and spent time diagnosing clobbered state and relocating to unique directories.
candidates.near_match_reason: The evidence shows shared workspace instability rather than a proven concurrent edit to one same file.

candidates.reason: Although shared temporary state was observed, no child is shown consuming a sibling-generated artifact as authoritative reference input; they detected the problem and relocated.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel parent delegated seven behavior-probing tasks and explicitly told children not to implement, but no later actor took ownership of writing the replacement executable.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parallel artifact had no buildable replacement implementation and failed compilation.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Pipeline ownership would apply after implementation ownership existed; here the implementation itself was unassigned.

retained_patterns.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing
retained_patterns.reason: The launched child agents were active when the run cancelled the turn, and their returned results all stated that they were stopped before finishing.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: No completed child reports were available to fold into implementation planning.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The missing reports were not completed verifier findings; the children were interrupted before finalization.

retained_patterns.reason: Several concurrent children used the same temporary probing path and observed unexpected or clobbered state from sibling activity.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The affected children had to abandon the shared temporary path and rebuild isolated probes, consuming task time and undermining provenance.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: No same-file edit race is directly proven; the concrete event is broader shared workspace instability.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Fan-out Budget Exhaustion was suppressed because the same timeout chain is more directly explained by missing implementation ownership and early child termination.
No Failure Takeover and Blind Timeout Wait were suppressed because no separate post-failure takeover or ignored-progress episode is visible.
Same-File Collision and overwrite labels were suppressed because the shared-state episode lacks proof of a specific file or final deliverable overwrite.
